messages:
Maya Chen: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-apps) reporting intermittent 429s when traffic fails over to eu-west during a multi-region surge. They say us-west stays healthy but when the client falls back to eu-west we see a burst of 429s for ~30s. They included a repro and logs, sharing below. Can eng-sre/eng-runtime triage? :wave:

Maya Chen: Repro curl they used (this toggles region via header):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxxx" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rw-13b","input":"ping"}'
```

Maya Chen: Snippet from customer request errors (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-05T14:12:07Z] req_id=R-8a3f client_ip=1.2.3.4 region_pref=us-west-2 routed_to=eu-west-1 status=429 err="region_quota_exceeded"
[2026-03-05T14:12:08Z] req_id=R-8a40 client_ip=1.2.3.4 region_pref=us-west-2 routed_to=eu-west-1 status=429 err="burst_credit_depleted"
[2026-03-05T14:12:15Z] req_id=R-8a41 client_ip=1.2.3.4 region_pref=us-west-2 routed_to=eu-west-1 status=200 latency_ms=78
[2026-03-05T14:12:39Z] req_id=R-8a42 client_ip=1.2.3.4 routed_to=eu-west-1 status=429 err="cross_region_throttle"
```

Maya Chen: Customer also saw increased token billing for those spikes and are worried about retries. They claim they were on an enterprise reserved plan with burst credits but still hit rages of 429s.

infra-bot: Alert: multi-region failover surge detected for acct=acme-apps at 2026-03-05T14:12:06Z — dropped_rate=18% across eu-west-1 cluster. Metric: regional_inflight > reserved_capacity + burst_credits.

Liam O'Connor: Thanks Maya. Leaving quick notes while I dig in. Two possible angles: (1) routing policy pushed many sessions into eu-west when us-west degraded (affinity disabled?), (2) eu-west had its burst_credit pool exhausted and routing fallback policy is "reject_on_overload" rather than queue. Need the full request-ids and the routing decision logs from the gateway. Can you paste one full request-id payload?

Maya Chen: Pasted one full trace for req_id=R-8a3f:
```
{"req_id":"R-8a3f","client":"acme-apps","orig_region":"us-west-2","routed_region":"eu-west-1","decision":"route_fallback","fallback_reason":"cap_exceeded_us-west","regional_capacity_at_route":0.92,"burst_pool_remaining":0}
```

Priya Singh: Quick context — the runtime exposes two important knobs: regional_burst_pool (shared across customers per region) and per_customer_burst_allowance. If shared regional_burst_pool hits 0 the fallback behavior depends on route_policy: either queue/slowstart or reject. For this account, I see route_policy=reject (older enterprise defaults). That would explain immediate 429s. Also we have a known warmup inefficiency when KV cache coldness intersects cross-zone latency — causes a sharp but short pressure spike.

Liam O'Connor: Does caller have affinity disabled? If they were sticky to us-west and then clients flip to eu-west, we might be double-allocating caches. Carlos, any billing flags here?

Carlos Vega: From CS side — they bought reserved capacity in us-west but expected failover to use dedicated reserved in eu-west (they did not purchase eu-west reserved). They assumed platform would queue rather than reject. They reported a billing blip where retry storms inflated token usage. We should be careful with guidance — they don't want silencers that cause huge backoffs.

Priya Singh: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Flip route_policy for this tenant to queue_on_overload for eu-west (risk: higher tail latency).
- Temporarily increase per_customer_burst_allowance for acme-apps in eu-west + top up regional_burst_pool by 50% for 2 mins.
- Enable regional_affinity for their sessions so new sessions prefer us-west until stabilized.

Priya Singh: How-to (ops commands):
```
# set per-tenant routing policy
redwoodctl tenants update acme-apps --region eu-west-1 --route-policy queue_on_overload

# temporarily top-up regional burst pool
redwoodctl region patch eu-west-1 --burst-topup 50 --duration 120

# enable affinity to reduce cross-zone allocation
redwoodctl tenants update acme-apps --regional-affinity true
```

Liam O'Connor: +1. Also request a small runtime patch to log the routing fallback reason in the token billing pipeline so we can correlate token counts to failover retries. I'll file a follow-up. For short repro: can someone simulate with a 2s us-west outage and 10k rps client with sticky=false? I can run a load test on staging.

Maya Chen: I've asked the customer for permission to perform canary top-up and to toggle their route policy. They approved top-up but asked we not change latency characteristics without explicit sign-off. They prefer queue_on_overload but only during the next maintenance window.

Priya Singh: Ok — we'll do the top-up immediately (low risk) and gather more traces. Liam, ping me when you run the staging load so I can capture runtime metrics (burst_pool, inflight, kv_hit_rate).

Liam O'Connor: Scheduling the sim at 2026-03-05T15:30Z on staging. Will push a tiny routing change: set route_policy to queue_on_overload for 10s in staging then revert. Aim is to reproduce the 30s 429 window.

Maya Chen: Customer update sent: we topped up burst credits and are monitoring. Asking if we can get a post-mortem explaining why reserved capacity didn't prevent failover 429s (they expected eu-west to be used as fallback without rejects).

Priya Singh: Action items captured:
- short: top-up regional burst pool (done), confirm logs and traces for req_ids R-8a3f..R-8a42 (Maya).
- medium: add billing correlation to routing fallback events (Liam).
- long: revisit enterprise defaults to prefer queue_on_overload rather than reject_on_overload for cross-region failovers (product + legal for billing implications).

Liam O'Connor: I'll open ENG-RT-1427 for the logging change and ENG-OPS-923 to run the staged resilience test.

infra-bot: Incident note appended to acct=acme-apps: temporary burst_topup applied at 2026-03-05T14:14:02Z by Priya Singh. Monitoring window 2m.

Carlos Vega: Thanks — I'll follow up with the customer on billing expectations and the PM to discuss defaults. :handshake: 

Maya Chen: Closing loop here, will paste additional traces once we have them. Thanks team.
